observations: Three photos show a small, curved sofa with a black frame and orange upholstery.
The sofa has a single seat cushion and no visible backrest or armrests beyond the curved frame.
The material appears to be vinyl or faux leather, with some sheen and minor creasing.
No brand or model markings are visible on the sofa or in the photos.
The sofa is photographed indoors, against a patterned curtain, with sunlight casting shadows.
No signs of major damage, tears, or stains are visible in the photos.

claims.evidence: All three photos show a sofa with orange upholstery and a design suitable for two people. The color is consistently orange/yellowish in all shots.

risks.risk: Hidden damage or wear not visible in photos, such as tears, stains, or structural issues under the seat or on the underside.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the underside and base of the sofa, and a photo showing the back and sides, especially under the seat cushion.
risks.if_unproven: priced as potentially damaged or worn, with lower value

risks.risk: Material is not genuine leather and may be low-quality vinyl or faux leather with poor durability.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the material texture and stitching, ideally with a finger pressing the surface to show flexibility and quality.
risks.if_unproven: priced as lower-grade material, reducing value

risks.risk: Sofa may not be structurally sound or may have loose joints or wobbling frame.
risks.proof: A video or photo showing the sofa being gently pressed or sat on to test stability.
risks.if_unproven: priced as potentially unstable, reducing value

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the underside and base of the sofa.
Close-up photo of the material texture and stitching.
Photo or video showing the sofa being sat on to test stability.
response.reason: The item is clearly a 2-seater sofa with orange upholstery, as claimed. While there are hidden risks related to material quality and structural integrity, these do not prevent pricing — the item can be priced at its worst-case condition (e.g., worn, low-grade material, unstable) based on visible evidence. The photos are sufficient to identify the item and support the claim.
